To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a time and dose‐dependent proteomic kinetic analysis revealed events such as decreased nucleotide and amino acid synthesis potentially associated with a cell cycle blockade, variations that may be associated with resistance acquisition, such over‐expressions of proteins such as aldehyde dehydrognase and both cytokeratin 8 and 19, and a potential increase in glycolysis, which could lead to an increase in the proliferating potential of IGROV‐1 cells.
we have identified proteins associated with the chemoresistance of the IGROV1 human ovarian cancer cell line to the cisplatin‐based chemotherapy.

we have identified proteins involved in the response of ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin, and that these proteins are potential biomarkers for the prediction and prevention of resistance to cisplatin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins involved in chemoresistance and could contribute to the discovery of new therapeutic targets for the management of chemoresistant ovarian cancer

identifying proteins associated with the acquisition of chemotherapeutic resistance and, thus, with the development of a proteomic tool that could help in the identification of new therapeutic targets for ovarian cancer treatment.
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying the emergence of cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer, which may lead to the identification of new therapeutic targets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our proteomic analysis of the IGROV1 response to CDDP treatment allowed us to identify a set of proteins whose expression was modified by the drug, and that could be involved in chemoresistance acquisition.
our results provide evidence that CDDP‐induced chemoresistance is associated with the modulation of a large number of proteins, which may be involved in the acquisition of this resistance.
the IGROV1 response to CDDP treatment is characterized by a complex and dynamic proteome, which could provide useful information to improve our understanding of CDDP‐resistance mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of proteomic analysis with kinetic study and statistical approach could be an effective strategy for the identification of potential markers of chemoresistance.
CDDP treatment of IGROV‐1 cells leads to an increase in proteins associated with resistance acquisition and to a decrease in proteins associated with apoptosis.

the combination of a proteomic analysis with a statistical approach allows the identification of proteins involved in the response of cancer cells to chemotherapy, and could help in understanding the mechanisms of chemoresistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proteomic analysis can be a valuable tool for identifying new biomarkers and targets for the design of novel therapeutic strategies against cancer.
the proteomic approach is a powerful and promising method to investigate mechanisms of drug response and resistance.
proteomic analysis can be a powerful tool for understanding the molecular mechanisms of chemoresistance in cancer cells.
